questions.Question: Which compartment of the ruminant stomach is physiologically equivalent to the monogastric (simple) stomach, secreting gastric juice, hydrochloric acid, and pepsin?
questions.OptionA: Abomasum (true stomach)
questions.OptionB: Omasum
questions.OptionC: Reticulum
questions.OptionD: Rumen
questions.Option_a: Abomasum (true stomach)
questions.Option_b: Omasum
questions.Option_c: Reticulum
questions.Option_d: Rumen
questions.Explanation: The abomasum is the glandular 'true' stomach of ruminants, secreting digestive enzymes (pepsin, rennin) and HCl to digest microbial protein and bypass nutrients.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.Question: In the avian (poultry) digestive tract, what is the specific physiological function of the muscular gizzard (ventriculus)?
questions.OptionA: Enzymatic secretion of bile and pancreatic amylase
questions.OptionB: Mechanical grinding and crushing of coarse grains and seeds with the aid of swallowed insoluble grit/stones
questions.OptionC: Temporary storage and moistening of swallowed whole grain seeds
questions.OptionD: Absorption of volatile fatty acids into the bloodstream
questions.Option_a: Enzymatic secretion of bile and pancreatic amylase
questions.Option_b: Mechanical grinding and crushing of coarse grains and seeds with the aid of swallowed insoluble grit/stones
questions.Option_c: Temporary storage and moistening of swallowed whole grain seeds
questions.Option_d: Absorption of volatile fatty acids into the bloodstream
questions.Explanation: Because birds lack teeth, the thick, muscular gizzard lined with a tough koilin membrane uses ingested grit/stones to grind tough grain kernels into fine mash.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.Question: What is the function of the 'crop' in the domestic chicken (Gallus domesticus)?
questions.OptionA: Chemical digestion of dietary proteins with hydrochloric acid
questions.OptionB: Grinding grains into a fine paste
questions.OptionC: Temporary storage, softening, and moistening of ingested feed before it passes to the proventriculus
questions.OptionD: Excretion of uric acid crystals from the kidneys
questions.Option_a: Chemical digestion of dietary proteins with hydrochloric acid
questions.Option_b: Grinding grains into a fine paste
questions.Option_c: Temporary storage, softening, and moistening of ingested feed before it passes to the proventriculus
questions.Option_d: Excretion of uric acid crystals from the kidneys
questions.Explanation: The crop is an outpocketing of the avian esophagus that stores grain food temporarily, softening it with saliva before passing it into the glandular proventriculus.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.Question: What unique anatomical feature allows young nursing calves and lambs to direct milk straight from the esophagus into the abomasum, bypassing the undeveloped rumen?
questions.OptionA: Ileocecal sphincter
questions.OptionB: Pyloric valve
questions.OptionC: Cecal appendix
questions.OptionD: Esophageal (reticular) groove
questions.Option_a: Ileocecal sphincter
questions.Option_b: Pyloric valve
questions.Option_c: Cecal appendix
questions.Option_d: Esophageal (reticular) groove
questions.Explanation: The esophageal groove is a muscular fold that closes reflexively during suckling, forming a conduit that channels milk directly to the abomasum, preventing microbial spoilage in the rumen.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.Question: Which pituitary hormone is responsible for triggering milk 'let-down' by stimulating the contraction of myoepithelial cells surrounding the alveoli in a dairy cow's udder?
questions.OptionA: Oxytocin
questions.OptionB: Prolactin
questions.OptionC: Progesterone
questions.OptionD: Estrogen
questions.Option_a: Oxytocin
questions.Option_b: Prolactin
questions.Option_c: Progesterone
questions.Option_d: Estrogen
questions.Explanation: Sensory stimulation of the teats (or milking sounds) causes the posterior pituitary to release oxytocin into the bloodstream, contracting myoepithelial cells and causing milk let-down.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.Question: Which organ in the female mammalian reproductive tract serves as the site of fertilization where the ovum meets the sperm?
questions.OptionA: Uterus (womb)
questions.OptionB: Fallopian tube (oviduct)
questions.OptionC: Cervix
questions.OptionD: Vagina
questions.Option_a: Uterus (womb)
questions.Option_b: Fallopian tube (oviduct)
questions.Option_c: Cervix
questions.Option_d: Vagina
questions.Explanation: Fertilization occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube (oviduct); the resulting zygote then travels down into the uterine horn for implantation.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science

questions.Question: Where is the hard calcium carbonate eggshell deposited on the developing avian egg?

questions.Option_d: Uterus (shell gland)

questions.Option_d: Storage of glycogen for physical running energy

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.Question: Which part of the ruminant stomach features numerous thin, leaf-like muscular laminae that reabsorb water and bicarbonate from the digesta?

questions.Explanation: The omasum contains broad parallel muscular leaves (manyplies) that absorb water, minerals, and volatile fatty acids, condensing digesta before it enters the abomasum.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science

questions.Question: In male farm animals, which accessory sex gland produces an alkaline, viscous pre-ejaculatory fluid that lubricates and flushes acidic urine from the urethra?

questions.Option_b: Thyroid gland

questions.Option_d: Bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands

questions.OptionB: The feed required to produce 30 liters of milk per day
questions.OptionC: The rich feed given to broilers during their final week before slaughter
questions.OptionD: A diet composed exclusively of mineral salt licks and clean water
questions.Option_a: The quantity of balanced feed required strictly to keep an animal alive and healthy at constant body weight without gain, loss, or production

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Animal Nutrition, Ration Formulation, and Feedstuffs
questions.Question: What feed additive is routinely added to laying hen diets to provide calcium essential for strong eggshell formation and prevention of cage layer fatigue?
questions.OptionA: Crushed oyster shell (or feed-grade limestone)

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Animal Nutrition, Ration Formulation, and Feedstuffs
questions.Question: What is the primary nutritional role of non-protein nitrogen (NPN) compounds like urea when fed in controlled amounts to adult ruminants?
questions.OptionA: Urea directly lubricates the ruminal papillae
questions.OptionB: Rumen microbes utilize the nitrogen from urea to synthesize high-quality microbial protein and amino acids
questions.OptionC: Urea eliminates internal roundworms from the abomasum
questions.OptionD: Urea provides instant metabolic glucose for energy

questions.Option_d: Urea provides instant metabolic glucose for energy
questions.Explanation: Rumen bacteria hydrolyze urea into ammonia, combining it with dietary carbohydrates to build high-quality bacterial protein that is digested downstream in the abomasum.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science

questions.Question: Why is it FATAL to feed urea to monogastric animals like pigs and poultry?
questions.OptionA: Monogastrics convert urea into pure nitric acid in the gizzard
questions.OptionB: Urea dissolves the intestinal lining within three minutes
questions.OptionC: Monogastrics lack the rumen microflora needed to utilize NPN, leading to rapid ammonia absorption, severe alkalosis, and death
questions.OptionD: Urea causes their body feathers to catch fire

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science

questions.Question: In ration formulation using the Pearson Square method, what is the required proportion of Maize (9% CP) and Groundnut Cake (45% CP) to formulate a diet containing 18% Crude Protein?
questions.OptionA: 18 parts Maize to 18 parts Groundnut Cake
questions.OptionB: 45 parts Maize to 9 parts Groundnut Cake
questions.OptionC: 10 parts Maize to 20 parts Groundnut Cake
questions.OptionD: 27 parts Maize to 9 parts Groundnut Cake (3:1 ratio)
questions.Option_a: 18 parts Maize to 18 parts Groundnut Cake
questions.Option_b: 45 parts Maize to 9 parts Groundnut Cake
questions.Option_c: 10 parts Maize to 20 parts Groundnut Cake
questions.Option_d: 27 parts Maize to 9 parts Groundnut Cake (3:1 ratio)

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Animal Nutrition, Ration Formulation, and Feedstuffs
questions.Question: Which nutritional metabolic disorder occurs in high-producing dairy cows around calving, caused by acute hypocalcemia (sudden calcium deficiency)?
questions.OptionA: Milk fever (parturient paresis)
questions.OptionB: Rickets
questions.OptionC: Ketosis (acetonemia)
questions.OptionD: Grass tetany
questions.Option_a: Milk fever (parturient paresis)
questions.Option_b: Rickets
questions.Option_c: Ketosis (acetonemia)
questions.Option_d: Grass tetany
questions.Explanation: Onset of copious colostrum secretion drains blood calcium faster than bones can mobilize it, causing acute hypocalcemia (milk fever), muscular tremors, and paralysis.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Animal Nutrition, Ration Formulation, and Feedstuffs
questions.Question: What nutritional disease is caused by acute magnesium deficiency in lactating cattle grazing lush spring pastures?
questions.OptionA: Rinderpest
questions.OptionB: Grass tetany (hypomagnesemia)
questions.OptionC: Milk fever
questions.OptionD: Scurvy
questions.Option_a: Rinderpest
questions.Option_b: Grass tetany (hypomagnesemia)
questions.Option_c: Milk fever
questions.Option_d: Scurvy
questions.Explanation: Grass tetany (lactation tetany) results from low blood magnesium when cattle graze lush, low-magnesium pastures, causing hyper-excitability, convulsions, and death.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Animal Nutrition, Ration Formulation, and Feedstuffs
questions.Question: What serious condition in ruminants is caused by excessive accumulation of fermentation gases (froth) in the rumen when animals overgraze lush young leguminous pastures?
questions.OptionA: Ketosis
questions.OptionB: Anthrax
questions.OptionC: Bloat (tympany)
questions.OptionD: Brucellosis
questions.Option_a: Ketosis
questions.Option_b: Anthrax
questions.Option_c: Bloat (tympany)
questions.Option_d: Brucellosis
questions.Explanation: Bloat occurs when soluble proteins in succulent legumes form a stable froth in the rumen, trapping fermentation gases (CO2, CH4) and exerting pressure on the lungs.

questions.Subject: Agricultural Science
questions.Topic: Animal Nutrition, Ration Formulation, and Feedstuffs

questions.Option_c: Palm kernel meal
questions.Option_d: Fish meal
questions.Explanation: Fish meal contains ~60–70% crude protein rich in essential lysine and methionine, as well as calcium and phosphorus, accelerating early chick growth.
